queries: OpenAI 800 million weekly active users DevDay October 2025
Altman GPT-5 rollout capacity crunch compute prioritize August 2025
AWS and OpenAI announce multi-year strategic partnership $38 billion

sources_considered.why: Reports Altman's August 2025 compute rationing and fleet expansion plans.
Primary announcement of a large new compute deal.
Shows added Google capacity; the AWS deal makes the same point more strongly.

receipt.public_excerpt: In August, OpenAI said it was on the cusp of reaching 700 million weekly active users, already an increase from 500 million weekly active users at the end of March.

evidence_items.explanation: User growth continued strongly after the post, from 500M to about 700M by August and 800M by October 2025, so the antecedent is met on a plain reading.

receipt.public_excerpt: We will then prioritize API demand up to the currently allocated capacity and commitments we've made to customers. (For a rough sense, we can support about an additional ~30% new API growth from where we are today with this capacity.)

evidence_items.explanation: After GPT-5's launch, OpenAI had to ration compute between user groups because of capacity limits, matching part (a).

receipt.public_excerpt: Under this new $38 billion agreement, which will have continued growth over the next seven years, OpenAI is accessing AWS compute comprising hundreds of thousands of state-of-the-art NVIDIA GPUs

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI secured access to hundreds of thousands of new GPUs from a non-Microsoft provider, which contradicts part (b), 'not much room to expand'.

receipt.public_excerpt: We are ~doubling our compute fleet over the next 5 months (!) so this situation should get better.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI said it was about to roughly double its compute fleet, against the claim that it had little room to expand.

unresolved_gaps: Whether OpenAI actually doubled its fleet in five months is a company claim, not independently measured.
'At this rate' is undefined, so whether the antecedent is fully met depends on the reading.
